title: The normalized source-isomorphism comparisons commute with the second mate
statement: Use the unchanged scheme, functor, adjunction and ordinary-base-change hypotheses of lem-sc-right-adjoint-mate-scheme-iso-transport-mate, assume r is an isomorphism, and supply natural isomorphisms φ and ψ for a,b along e and d,b′ along r, each satisfying the counit normalization of lem-sc-scheme-iso-right-adjoint-normalized. For every supplied ordinary invertibility family hβf, define s by canonical pullback composition along r and pullback.fst f g, the first projection equation, inverse composition along pullback.fst f′ g and e.hom, and pullback of φK. Then s.hom≫the ambient f′ second mate at K equals the r-pullback of the ambient f second mate at K followed by ψ at LgK. This is an equality for specified comparisons; it supplies neither comparison existence nor an arrow isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the inverse ordinary square presentation of the fixed second mate. Apply the ordinary source-isomorphism transport theorem to obtain k, q, σ with their fixed component formulas and q invertible.

Lift the supplied φ and ψ to the full quasi-coherent subcategories. Their normalization hypotheses, rewritten with the supplied component formulas for k and q, give the two counit identities. Use schemeIso_liftedComparison_counit for the upper vertical map to pass its supplied normalization to the lifted comparison. The q formula is already postcomposed and reassociated. Transpose the desired mate square under adjb′, precompose by q, use ordinary-square transport, naturality and the two counit identities, and cancel q. This is the proved private categorical calculation source_iso_mate_comparison. Rewrite the inverse-square mates back to the fixed second mates and use the specified component of σ to identify the source comparison exactly.
